verdict.line: You lose if you chase Gnar's pokes on cooldown; you win if you force Mega Gnar to fight you at point-blank range.

brief.thesis: Gnar wins at range with Boomerang Throw poke and Hop mobility, but Sett's E (Facebreaker) only needs enemies on opposite sides to stun — meaning once Mega Gnar triggers and Hyper/Wallop ends, Sett can pull him in through minions and remove his kiting advantage entirely. The 47.2% win rate over 248 games reflects how often Sett players get worn down before that window opens, not an unwinnable lane.

theirWindow.when: Mini Gnar, Boomerang Throw off cooldown
theirWindow.what: Gnar will throw Boomerang Throw (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown) to poke and slow from 1100 range, then disengage with Hop. Do not walk forward to trade here; W (Haymaker) stores the damage you take as Grit, so eating one boomerang isn't free damage lost, it's shield banked for later.

yourWindow.when: Mega Gnar transforms, Wallop on cooldown
yourWindow.what: The moment Rage maxes and Gnar transforms, his W becomes Wallop (a ground-smash stun with its own cooldown) instead of ranged Hyper. Walk him down immediately after he uses Wallop and land E (Facebreaker) by catching him between you and a minion wave or jungle wall to force the stun, then dump stored Grit with W.

start.why: 52.3% win rate over 193 games; the flat damage reduction on the first attack from each enemy directly blunts Gnar's auto-poke while you're stuck walking into Boomerang Throw range.

boots.why: 48.7% win rate over 197 games at 70.1% pick rate; the attack-damage reduction on basic attacks matters most against Gnar's auto-reset harass pattern once he's Hyper.

core.why: Closes the gap Gnar opens with Hop; the slow-on-hit is how you actually catch a kiting target before your W Grit shield wears off.
60% win rate over 40 games on this path; shred helps you kill through Mega Gnar's added survivability before his transform runs out.
The missing-health regen on Sett's passive stacks with this item's sustain, letting you re-engage Gnar's poke lane after a bad trade instead of backing off.

situational.when: he is landing Boomerang Throw consistently and you need burst-damage survivability to close distance without dying first
the lane stabilizes and you are winning side-lane 1v1s, since it rewards split-pushing a lane Gnar can't contest in melee
he is building into sustained poke damage over burst and you need raw HP to out-sustain his Rage-building autos

runes.keystoneWhy: You are forced into extended skirmishes to catch a kiting target, not quick burst trades; Conqueror's stacking adaptive damage and healing rewards staying on top of Gnar once your E lands instead of a one-shot window you won't get.

summoners.why: Flash+Ghost is run in 40.4% of games (18.7% pick rate) and is the better fit here over the Ignite line: Ghost closes the gap on a kiting ranged champion that Ignite alone won't let you catch, and Flash covers your E engage or lets you dodge a point-blank Hop bounce.

playing.title: Never auto-trade into Boomerang Throw range
playing.detail: Gnar's Q is 1100 range with a 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown; standing in that threat range to farm invites free pokes you cannot return. Hold minion-wave position just outside it instead.

playing.title: Bank Grit before engaging
playing.detail: W (Haymaker) stores all damage you take as Grit passively; let a boomerang or two land on you before you commit, so your shield-and-punch is actually large when you cast it.

playing.title: E through the wave, not around it
playing.detail: Facebreaker stuns only if Gnar is sandwiched between you and something else on the opposite side; walking minions into position before you commit the engage turns a slow into a stun.

playing.title: Punish post-Wallop, not pre-transform
playing.detail: Mega Gnar's W becomes a ground-smash stun on its own cooldown; baiting that stun out and whiffing it, then closing immediately, is your clean engage window since he has no ranged poke left until Rage resets.

playing.title: Respect GNAR! near walls at level 6+
playing.detail: R throws everyone in a chosen direction and stuns anyone who hits a wall for bonus damage; don't extend fights near jungle walls once he has ultimate up, even off-cooldown late (it drops to 0s cooldown at rank 4-5).

playing.title: Use Ghost to force fights, not just to flee
playing.detail: Since Gnar's whole kit survives on kiting space, Ghost is for closing distance proactively when his Hop is down, not only for disengaging a losing trade.

playing.title: Side-push once Stridebreaker is online
playing.detail: Gnar has no answer to a melee duelist in a side lane without minion cover to bounce off of; if the lane is even by level 10-ish, shift pressure to split-push with Hullbreaker rather than forcing more river trades.

brief.patchCaveat: The build path, runes, summoner spells, and all win-rate figures above are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the tactical reading of cooldown windows and engage timing is our own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep your distance to avoid being kited by Gnar. Keep Mega Gnar’s (R) in mind while fighting him.
